audit_findings.title: The FY2024 earnings anchor is stale and predates a known financing change
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 continuing income was $597 million versus $669 million in FY2024; first-half 2026 continuing income fell $133 million to $211 million and free cash flow fell $222 million to negative $36 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor directly scales forecast owner earnings and operating present value; interest expense is retained because this is equity-level OE
audit_findings.evidence: The agreements include a total $ 400 million notional amount maturing in February 2025 with a weighted average fixed interest rate of 4.63 % and a total $ 300 million notional amount maturing in February 2026 with a weighted average fixed interest rate of 4.23 %.
audit_findings.explanation: Using FY2024 as the latest actual is a demonstrated dating error because the supplied FY2025 10-K was available. The specific claim that hedge expiration increased interest is not demonstrated: filed interest expense declined from $238 million in 2024 to $224 million in 2025 and from $115 million to $108 million in the first half of 2026. Nevertheless, materially weaker 2026 earnings and cash flow make the stale anchor reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion. Direction is mixed because lower operating results point downward while lower interest expense points upward.
audit_findings.action: Construct FY2025 and trailing-twelve-month June 2026 OE from the filed statements using the original OE rules, reconcile actual post-hedge interest expense, and rerun all scenarios with the latest qualifying actual anchor.

audit_findings.title: The MEKO investment may be counted in both owner earnings and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2024 equity-method earnings were $8 million; if fully embedded in the anchor, the computed base-case effect is approximately $112 million, $0.44 per share, or $0.31 on the 30%-MOS buy-below price
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method earnings would enter OE while the separately valued MEKO stake also enters the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: We record our equity in the net earnings of Mekonomen on a one quarter lag.
audit_findings.explanation: Double counting remains an unresolved possibility because the OE normalization bridge was not supplied. However, the maximum directly evidenced FY2024 overlap is $8 million, only 1.2% of the $648.8 million anchor. At the supplied base operating-value-to-anchor ratio, removing it would lower the buy-below price by about $0.31, less than the existing $0.70 gap between $26.24 and the $25.54 market price. It therefore would not independently change the stated buy conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2024 OE bridge for removal of the $8 million equity-method earnings and the $5 million dividend, and confirm the separately added stake against its latest filed carrying and market values; correct the rerun if either item remains in OE.

audit_findings.title: A rising intangible-amortization add-back may omit acquisition-like maintenance reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2024 intangible amortization was $182 million, equal to 28.1% of the $648.8 million OE anchor; the maintenance-reinvestment portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back amortization raises OE, while omitting recurring acquisition or replacement spending leaves the related economic depletion uncharged
audit_findings.evidence: Amortization expense for intangibles was $ 182 million, $ 126 million, and $ 95 million during the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large amortization expense and an acquisition-based business model, but it does not demonstrate that any particular amount is maintenance spending. Even so, an annual adjustment of only about $18.2 million would eliminate the $0.70 buy-below cushion under the supplied base valuation. That is roughly 10% of the $182 million add-back, so the unresolved maintenance component is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Disaggregate the FY2024 amortization add-back by customer relationships, technology, trade names and internal software; estimate sustaining acquisition and replacement spending from filed acquisition cash flows and operating evidence, then rerun OE with the supportable maintenance portion deducted.

audit_findings.title: The synthetic leases create a claim not yet represented in FY2024 earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $100 million construction cost, $35 million aggregate future lease commitment and a 100% residual-value guarantee
audit_findings.mechanism: Commenced rent would reduce future OE; an enforceable residual shortfall could become an equity-bridge claim
audit_findings.evidence: Each lease arrangement contains a residual value guarantee of 100 % of the total construction cost.
audit_findings.explanation: This was a disclosed forward-looking commitment rather than a demonstrated FY2024 omission: the facilities were under construction and the leases had not commenced. Even stacking the filed $100 million construction exposure and $35 million lease commitment produces $135 million, equivalent to about $0.37 on the MOS-adjusted per-share threshold, below the existing $0.70 cushion. The exposure should still be monitored because commencement determines recurring rent and recognized liabilities.
audit_findings.action: Confirm each facility's completion and lease commencement status as of September 5, 2026, obtain the recorded ROU assets and liabilities and annual rent, and revisit the valuation if actual residual exposure or sustaining rent exceeds the filed commitments.

audit_findings.title: Supplier-finance working-capital releases could be mistaken for recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: In FY2024, $871 million of invoices were confirmed and $840 million were paid, a computed $31 million financing-related increase before the $26 million adverse currency effect; if fully treated as recurring OE, the computed base-case effect is approximately $436 million, $1.71 per share, or $1.20 on the buy-below price
audit_findings.mechanism: Extended payment terms increase operating cash flow and working-capital-derived OE without representing recurring operating profit
audit_findings.evidence: We utilize voluntary supply chain finance programs to support our efforts in negotiating payment term extensions with suppliers as part of our effort to improve our operating cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence of the financing program and the $31 million pre-currency increase are demonstrated; whether the OE bridge normalized that increase is unresolved. A $31 million recurring-credit error exceeds the approximately $18.2 million annual OE reduction needed to erase the $0.70 buy-below cushion, so it is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2024 OE working-capital adjustments to the supplier-finance rollforward, separate foreign-exchange movement from confirmations less payments, remove any one-time term-extension benefit, and rerun all scenarios if the $31 million or another financing release was credited to recurring OE.

audit_findings.title: The FY2024 anchor may retain a favorable legal-settlement benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $35 million pretax in the later filing, approximately $25.0 million after tax using the filed 28.7% FY2024 effective tax rate; computed base-case effect is approximately $351 million, $1.37 per share, or $0.96 on the buy-below price
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring settlement credit increases FY2024 net income and OE, which is then capitalized through the forecast and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in Selling, general and administrative expense primarily reflects unfavorable impacts of (i) $71 million from personnel costs excluding incentive compensation primarily due to the acquisition of Uni-Select, (ii) $36 million from facility costs primarily due to the acquisition of Uni-Select, (iii) $11 million from increased freight, vehicle, and fuel costs, partially offset by (iv) $42 million from lower incentive compensation, (v) $27 million from 38 professional fees primarily related to proceeds from the favorable settlement of a legal claim in 2024, (vi) $6 million from lower charitable contributions in the prior year period, and (vii) other individually immaterial factors representing an $11 million favorable impact in the aggregate.
audit_findings.explanation: The favorable settlement is demonstrated, but its retention in OE is only an unresolved possibility because the normalization bridge was not supplied. If retained, its computed after-tax effect would exceed the approximately $18.2 million annual OE reduction needed to erase the $0.70 buy-below cushion. It therefore could reverse the stated buy-below conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2024 OE bridge for an explicit after-tax removal of the legal-settlement credit; if absent, reduce anchor OE by the supportable after-tax amount and rerun every scenario and the buy-below calculation.
